title: Microservices Architecture with PEGA Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of microservices architecture patterns and implementation in PEGA

questions.question: Which principle is fundamental to microservices architecture?
options: Single Responsibility - each service owns a specific business capability
All services must share the same database
Services should be tightly coupled for performance
All services must use the same technology stack
questions.explanation: Single Responsibility is a key principle where each microservice owns a specific business capability, enabling independent development and deployment.

questions.question: In PEGA, what is the recommended approach for service decomposition?
options: Decompose by technical layers (UI, business logic, data)
Decompose by business capability and Case Types
Create one service per database table
questions.explanation: Service boundaries in PEGA should align with business capabilities and Case Types, encapsulating complete business functionality including data, logic, and interfaces.

questions.question: Which pattern is best for managing distributed transactions across PEGA microservices?
questions.explanation: The Saga Pattern manages distributed transactions by coordinating local transactions and using compensating transactions to maintain consistency when failures occur.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of implementing the Database per Service pattern?
questions.explanation: Database per Service ensures that each service owns its data, enabling service independence, loose coupling, and independent evolution of data models.

questions.question: Which PEGA component is best suited for implementing service-to-service communication?
questions.explanation: Service Rules and Connect Rules provide the necessary functionality for implementing REST APIs and HTTP-based communication between PEGA microservices.

questions.question: What is the purpose of implementing circuit breaker patterns in microservices?
options: To prevent cascading failures and provide resilience
questions.explanation: Circuit breaker patterns monitor service health and fail fast when services are unavailable, preventing cascading failures and providing system resilience.

questions.question: Which approach is recommended for monitoring PEGA microservices?
options: Implement distributed tracing and centralized logging
questions.explanation: Distributed tracing and centralized logging provide comprehensive visibility into microservices interactions, enabling effective monitoring and troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is a key consideration for PEGA microservices deployment?
options: Deploy all services together as a single unit
Each service should have its own deployment pipeline and versioning
Use the same version for all services
questions.explanation: Each microservice should have its own independent deployment pipeline and versioning strategy, enabling autonomous development and deployment cycles.
